source.notes: Synthesis of open GitHub datasets, FODMAP Friendly's public checklist, Open Food Facts taxonomy/ingredient tags, Wikipedia (CC BY-SA), Monash's public label-reading rules and registered-dietitian blogs summarizing the Monash and FODMAP Friendly apps. No dataset was bulk-copied: every GitHub food list found is second- or third-hand Monash data with no or restrictive licensing, so they were used to cross-check ratings and mine aliases; ratings below are recorded where at least two independent public sources agree, and disagreements are spelled out in notes. Foods with 'null' ratings are untested or ingredient-dependent and should be handled by ingredient-keyword flagging. Serving strings are as published by the cited source (ml/g/household measure). Lactose ratings apply to lactose-sensitive users only.

datasets.name: ts-sz/fodmap-data (mirror of gut-check)
datasets.license: MIT (code and JSON structure); README says underlying food data 'originates from Monash University research'
datasets.provenance: Weekly auto-extract of gut-check/gut-check.github.io (MIT) foodData/foodDetails; gut-check's FODMAP_RESEARCH.md cites Monash app, Gourmend, A Little Bit Yummy, The IBS Dietitian per row
datasets.why: Cleanest schema found (level, serving, portion thresholds low/moderate/high, fodmap_types, alternatives); 16 alcohol, 23 beverage, 38 condiment rows. Values are Monash-derived via secondary sources, so used here for cross-checking and portion thresholds, not bulk-copied. Some evident errors (rum 'low', beer 'moderate').

datasets.name: gut-check/gut-check.github.io
datasets.license: MIT (README); no LICENSE file in tree
datasets.provenance: Single-file PWA; food DB embedded in index.html; FODMAP_RESEARCH.md logs per-food sources (Monash app, Gourmend, A Little Bit Yummy, The IBS Dietitian)
datasets.why: Upstream of ts-sz; research log is a useful documented cross-check of portion thresholds. Same Monash-derivation caveat.

datasets.name: oseparovic/fodmap_list
datasets.license: None declared (all rights reserved by default)
datasets.provenance: Community-compiled; README lists 10 public handout sources (ibsdiets.org, Kate Scarlata, Diet vs Disease, Stanford handout, IBS Group brochure, etc.) and says items are only added when cross-referenced across several sources
datasets.why: Largest community JSON (69 stars, 12 categories incl. 34 drinks, 23 sweeteners, 28 condiments, 47 cooking ingredients); per-group 0/1/2 scores. No license - cross-check only, do not redistribute verbatim. Only binary low/high; qty sparse; some errors (HFCS tagged as oligos).

datasets.name: scottenock/fodmap-foss
datasets.provenance: src/data/fodmap.ts uses oseparovic's exact schema (id/name/fodmap/category/details) - a relicensed copy of that dataset
datasets.why: Duplicate of oseparovic data under GPL; nothing new.

datasets.name: GoodPigeon/FODMAP
datasets.provenance: Norwegian translation of oseparovic fodmap_repo.json (file named fodmap_repo_NO.json)
datasets.why: Duplicate/translation; not needed.

datasets.name: fodmap-diet/basket
datasets.provenance: Community PRs; per-item 'source' requested in PR template but not stored in JSON
datasets.why: MIT, per-letter JSON with low/medium/high, 'condition' (e.g. 'max 2 tbsp/day') and notes; 38 drinks, 35 condiments. No FODMAP groups, several dubious ratings (amaranth flour high, almond meal high). Cross-check only.

datasets.name: jvnn/fodmap-guide
datasets.provenance: 2013 Android app data.json, author disclaims accuracy
datasets.why: Non-standard JSON (uses '=' not ':'), 2013-era ratings that contradict current data (soft cheese avoid, sorbitol level 0); too old.

datasets.name: kwpav/fodsearch-api
datasets.provenance: Hand-compiled ingredients.csv; no sources cited; categories mirror Monash app layout
datasets.why: MIT; useful safe/moderate split incl. dairy alternatives and condiments; 'moderate' seems to mean 'has a serving limit'. Cross-check only.

datasets.name: zarhaselene/fodmap-recipe
datasets.provenance: App demo data; no sources
datasets.why: Small, no license, whole foods only; nothing not covered elsewhere.

datasets.name: jade-hernandez/guide-monf
datasets.license: None (docs/dataset-provenance.md explicitly records that license and provenance are unresolved)
datasets.provenance: 104 French records each stamped 'Monash University 2024' with no acquisition record; owner says assembled from public online info
datasets.why: Its own provenance audit says it cannot be redistributed; likely Monash app values. Excluded. Notable as a model of honest provenance documentation.

datasets.name: melaniehuang/fodmap-web (also hugomd/fodmap-react copy)
datasets.provenance: 2016 personal project; categories match Monash app; no sources
datasets.why: Good alias lists (e.g. bok choy spellings), 32 sweeteners, 24 condiments, edible yes/no plus limit text. GPL and no groups; cross-check and alias mining only.

datasets.name: timbenniks/fodmap-listr
datasets.provenance: en.json/nl.json Allowed/Not Allowed list, category ids; includes a 'Prebiotic Foods' category
datasets.why: Binary allowed/not allowed, no license; only skimmed (count not extracted).

datasets.name: ensadi/FOODS
datasets.provenance: Flat Food/Disposition/Classification JSON, no sources
datasets.why: MIT, US-centric names (half and half, deli slices); no servings/groups. Alias/cross-check only.

datasets.name: sergiorua/alexa-fodmap
datasets.provenance: high/low YAML lists, UK terms, no sources
datasets.why: Binary lists with UK naming (mange tout, choko); GPL. Skimmed only.

datasets.name: gautham50050/Fodmap-scanner
datasets.provenance: Header says compiled from Monash published categories, peer-reviewed composition studies, USDA/AFCD; it is an ingredient-substring table for parsing OFF/USDA ingredient lists
datasets.why: Most relevant open artifact for this app: 230 lowercase ingredient-list substrings with status, FODMAP group and severity weight, plus negation-style 'low' entries. Directly informed ingredientKeywords. MIT. Also has an OFF client (src/services/openFoodFacts.js).

datasets.name: nathaliatg/safe
datasets.provenance: Hand-written explanations with portion guidance, no citations
datasets.why: Best plain-language condiment/drink notes (worcestershire, sriracha, coconut aminos, hibiscus); no license so used as a cross-check/notes source only.

datasets.name: arran4/awesome-fodmap-resources
datasets.provenance: Link list
datasets.why: No food data; useful index of blogs/apps by country.

datasets.name: IBPA/FODMAPsAndGutMicrobiome
datasets.provenance: Meta-analysis code/metadata for microbiome studies
datasets.why: Not a food-rating dataset.

datasets.name: Kaggle / Hugging Face
datasets.provenance: Searched both; no FODMAP-specific dataset found. Hugging Face hosts openfoodfacts/product-database (ODbL) which is the full OFF dump
datasets.why: Nothing FODMAP-specific exists on either platform as of 2026-09-17; OFF dump on HF is the only adjacent asset.

datasets.name: FODMAP Friendly - Low FODMAP Foods Checklist (PDF)
datasets.license: Copyright Fodmap Pty Ltd, July 2021; no reuse license
datasets.provenance: FODMAP Friendly's own lab-tested program, summary handout
datasets.why: Publicly distributed handout with per-category serve sizes (grains 1/2 cup, vegetables 75 g, fruit 150 g, cheese 40 g, yoghurt 200 g, nuts 30 g, tea 250 ml, golden syrup 1 tsp). Independent of Monash, so valuable as a second lab-tested source. Only ~95 foods and no per-FODMAP breakdown; facts (not layout) used.

datasets.name: FODMAP Friendly certified products list
datasets.license: Proprietary; no API or reuse terms
datasets.provenance: Lab-tested certified packaged products with max serve size, filterable by country/brand/category
datasets.why: Site (including /wp-json/) is behind a Cloudflare managed challenge - 403 to every fetcher used. Not scrapeable without a browser; data is proprietary anyway. Recommend linking users to it rather than ingesting.

datasets.name: Open Food Facts
datasets.license: ODbL 1.0 (data) / DbCL (contents) / CC BY-SA (images); attribution required, share-alike for derived databases
datasets.provenance: Crowd-sourced packaged-food database; ingredients parsed against a taxonomy
datasets.why: No FODMAP rating fields. Label tags en:low-fodmap (5 products) and en:monash-university-low-fodmap-certified (4 products) are negligible. Value is the parsed ingredients array and additives_tags for keyword flagging: en:e420 sorbitol 21,048 products, en:high-fructose-corn-syrup 26,623, en:garlic-powder 4,821, en:e421 mannitol 1,656. Strict rate limits (product 100/min per docs, search 10/min; got HTML 'busy' pages at ~6 s spacing).

datasets.name: Spoonful blog: Top 45 FODMAP ingredients in packaged foods
datasets.license: Editorial content, copyright Spoonful; facts used, text not copied
datasets.provenance: Derived from Spoonful's scan of 600,000+ grocery labels; app data itself is proprietary
datasets.why: Best public ranking of which FODMAP ingredients actually appear on US labels; drove keyword priorities.

datasets.name: Monash FODMAP blog: Label reading and FODMAPs
datasets.license: Copyright Monash University; public educational post; facts used only
datasets.provenance: Primary authority
datasets.why: Authoritative rules for ingredient parsing: onion/garlic/inulin/FOS/GOS are avoid regardless of position; polyols (E420/421/953/965/966/967) and excess-fructose sweeteners are position-dependent; lactose list. Rules, not the app database, were used.

datasets.name: Wikipedia: FODMAP / Low-FODMAP diet
datasets.provenance: Cites Monash 2012 guidelines and peer-reviewed reviews
datasets.why: Freely licensed group-level lists (fructan, GOS, polyol sources; artificial polyols isomalt/maltitol/mannitol/sorbitol/xylitol). No servings.

datasets.name: Dietitian/educational blogs (A Little Bit Yummy, The IBS Dietitian, FODMAP Everyday, Keren Reiser, fodzyme, Gourmend, wholeisticliving, Casa de Sante, CDHF, InnerBuddies)
datasets.license: Copyright each publisher; facts used, wording not copied
datasets.provenance: Registered dietitians summarizing Monash and FODMAP Friendly app entries with servings
datasets.why: Only public source of serving-level detail for alcohol, teas, plant milks, sweeteners, condiments. Second-hand Monash data; individual entries disagree (kombucha, molasses, Greek yogurt) and disagreements are recorded in notes.

datasets.name: Fodmapedia
datasets.license: Proprietary (freemium app); started from Canadian Nutrient File
datasets.provenance: Monash, papers, USDA/Ciqual/AFCD, expert books
datasets.why: No API or export; premium-gated.

datasets.name: Google Sheet 'Monash FODMAP rip-off [compact] v2.4.0'
datasets.license: Unauthorized copy of Monash app data
datasets.provenance: Self-described rip-off of the Monash app
datasets.why: Verbatim Monash copy; export returned HTTP 400 (not publicly exportable). Deliberately not used.

datasets.name: Reddit r/FODMAPS wiki
datasets.provenance: Community
datasets.why: Reddit returns 403 to non-browser fetchers (old.reddit.com blocked by the tool, www.reddit.com .json endpoint 403). Not reviewed.

datasets.name: Fody Foods / Casa de Sante educational lists
datasets.provenance: Brand blogs; Fody's grocery list is a gated PDF, Casa de Sante soft-drink post is text
datasets.why: Casa de Sante soft-drink post gave usable serving numbers (espresso 2 oz, cranberry 8 oz, tomato juice 6 oz, OJ 3 oz). Fody page only describes categories; PDF not fetched.

foods.name: beer
foods.notes: Fructans in barley/wheat are largely fermented out; low at 375 ml per several dietitian summaries of the Monash app. Contains gluten. Community datasets disagree: oseparovic low, ts-sz/gut-check 'moderate', nathaliatg 'high' - the dietitian sources are the better-supported reading. Carbonation and alcohol are gut irritants independent of FODMAPs.

foods.name: gluten-free beer
foods.notes: Low in every source that lists it (ts-sz, CDHF, nathaliatg). Check label for added fruit juice or honey.

foods.name: wheat beer
foods.notes: Not separately reported in any public source; beer generally tested low. Treat as beer but flag as untested.

foods.name: stout
foods.notes: Not separately reported; beer class tested low. Untested style - flag rather than assume.

foods.name: non-alcoholic beer
foods.notes: Untested. Fermentation may be arrested earlier so residual fructans could be higher than regular beer; some brands add sugar or juice.

foods.name: red wine
foods.notes: Low at 150 ml. A Little Bit Yummy notes excess fructose becomes limiting at larger serves.

foods.name: white wine
foods.notes: Low at 150 ml in all sources. Dry styles have less residual sugar than sweet.

foods.name: rose wine
foods.notes: Low at 150 ml (kerenreiser, ts-sz, theibsdietitian).

foods.name: sparkling wine
foods.notes: Low at 150 ml in A Little Bit Yummy, FODMAP Everyday, ts-sz. CDHF lists 'sparkling wine' as avoid (fructose) - a minority view, likely referring to sweet sparkling styles. Carbonation is a separate irritant.

foods.name: sweet wine
foods.notes: Higher residual sugar (35-120 g/L) means excess fructose. ts-sz rates 'moderate' at 1 glass; FODMAP Everyday, kerenreiser and CDHF rate dessert wines high. Alcohol also slows fructose absorption.

foods.name: port
foods.notes: Fortified wine with high residual fructose - high per theibsdietitian and FODMAP Everyday; ts-sz 'moderate' at a small glass.

foods.name: sherry
foods.notes: Sweet/fortified sherry is high in fructose per Monash-derived summaries (theibsdietitian, kerenreiser).

foods.name: dry sherry
foods.notes: ts-sz/gut-check list dry sherry as low at a small glass; only one community source, treat with caution.

foods.name: ice wine
foods.notes: Dessert wine; high excess fructose (A Little Bit Yummy citing NUTTAB sugar data, kerenreiser).

foods.name: marsala
foods.notes: Listed with port as a high-fructose dessert wine by FODMAP Everyday.

foods.name: mulled wine
foods.notes: Untested. Usually red wine plus sugar or honey, orange and spices; honey-sweetened versions carry excess fructose.

foods.name: vodka
foods.notes: Distilled; low in every source. Flavored vodkas may contain added sugars/juice - check.

foods.name: gin
foods.notes: Low in every source. Pink/flavored gins may add fruit or sweeteners.

foods.name: whiskey
foods.notes: Low in every source (distillation removes fructans from grain mash). Honey- or flavored whiskeys are different products.

foods.name: brandy
foods.notes: Low at 30 ml (A Little Bit Yummy, FODMAP Everyday, theibsdietitian).

foods.name: tequila
foods.notes: Agave sugars are fermented and distilled away; low per Monash-derived summaries (gold and silver both listed by FODMAP Everyday). Mezcal not separately tested.

foods.name: rum
foods.notes: Every dietitian source reports Monash rates rum high in excess fructose (sugarcane/molasses base). ts-sz/gut-check lists rum 'low' - treat that as an error. Spiced/flavored rums add sugar.

foods.name: sake
foods.notes: Junmai sake low at 85 ml per FODMAP Everyday (Monash). Sweet/nigori styles untested.

foods.name: hard cider
foods.notes: Made from apples (high fructose + sorbitol); not formally tested per A Little Bit Yummy, which cites brewing research showing residual sugar alcohols. Rated high by inference across sources. Dry ciders lower in residual sugar but still untested.

foods.name: pear cider
foods.notes: Pears are high in fructose and sorbitol; inferred high, untested.

foods.name: hard seltzer
foods.notes: Untested. Typically fermented cane sugar or vodka plus natural flavor; check for fruit juice concentrate, HFCS or sugar alcohols. Carbonated.

foods.name: cream liqueur
foods.notes: Untested. Contains cream (lactose) and sugar; lactose-sensitive users should flag. Not in any public dataset.

foods.name: fruit liqueur
foods.notes: Untested. High sugar; some use HFCS or fruit juice concentrates. A Little Bit Yummy warns sweetened spirits may contain HFCS, honey, agave or sugar alcohols.

foods.name: premixed alcoholic drink
foods.notes: Ingredient-dependent: fruit juice, HFCS and sugar alcohols are common. Flag for label check.

foods.name: soju
foods.notes: CDHF lists soju under drinks to avoid (fructose), without a serving. No other source; treat as unverified.

foods.name: mead
foods.notes: Fermented honey; residual honey sugars give excess fructose. Inferred, untested.

foods.name: water
foods.notes: Universal low.

foods.name: sparkling water
foods.notes: Low; carbonation itself can cause bloating. Flavored versions: check for fruit juice concentrate or polyols.

foods.name: coffee
foods.notes: Low FODMAP (black, regular or decaf) in every source; caffeine is a gut stimulant so many sources cap at 1-3 cups. Milk/creamer adds lactose.

foods.name: espresso
foods.notes: Low per Casa de Sante summary of Monash (2 oz).

foods.name: instant coffee
foods.notes: Low at 2 tsp (Casa de Sante); oseparovic caveat: only if not blended with lactose/other FODMAPs (3-in-1 sachets often contain milk solids).

foods.name: decaf coffee
foods.notes: Listed as low alongside regular coffee (oseparovic).

foods.name: black tea
foods.notes: Weak black tea low; strong brew moderate (wholeisticliving citing Monash) or high (oseparovic). Fructans leach with longer steeping.

foods.name: green tea
foods.notes: Low at 250 ml in every source.

foods.name: white tea
foods.notes: Low at 250 ml.

foods.name: oolong tea
foods.notes: High in fructans in every source that lists it (ts-sz, oseparovic, melaniehuang, wholeisticliving).

foods.name: chai tea
foods.notes: Weak chai low; strong chai moderate-high because spice fructans extract with steeping. Cafe chai lattes usually add regular milk (lactose) and sometimes honey.

foods.name: matcha
foods.notes: Low at 1 tsp, moderate at 4 tsp (fructans) per wholeisticliving summary of Monash.

foods.name: chamomile tea
foods.notes: High fructans in ts-sz, oseparovic, melaniehuang, wholeisticliving; nathaliatg allows a weak 1-2 minute cup - minority view.

foods.name: fennel tea
foods.notes: High fructans (oseparovic, melaniehuang, wholeisticliving).

foods.name: dandelion tea
foods.notes: Strong dandelion tea high in fructans; oseparovic lists weak brew as low. Dandelion root 'coffee' substitutes likewise high.

foods.name: chicory coffee
foods.notes: Chicory root is one of the most concentrated inulin sources; CDHF and Spoonful list it as avoid.

foods.name: peppermint tea
foods.notes: Low in every source; peppermint may relax the lower esophageal sphincter (reflux).

foods.name: ginger tea
foods.notes: Low. Commercial ginger tea bags may blend chamomile/licorice - check.

foods.name: rooibos tea
foods.notes: Low in all sources.

foods.name: licorice root tea
foods.notes: Low per wholeisticliving citing Monash (10-15 min brew).

foods.name: hibiscus tea
foods.notes: Conflicting: wholeisticliving 'untested, likely low'; nathaliatg 'moderate fructans, steep <3 min'. Acidic. Leave unrated.

foods.name: yerba mate
foods.notes: Untested; clinical impression 'likely low' (wholeisticliving). Caffeinated.

foods.name: lemongrass tea
foods.notes: Low per wholeisticliving citing Monash.

foods.name: kombucha
foods.notes: Portion-dependent: low at 180 ml, high at 250 ml (fructans, excess fructose) per wholeisticliving and nathaliatg citing Monash; older lists (oseparovic, ts-sz, CDHF) simply rate it high. Sugar content and flavorings vary by brand; also histamine/caffeine.

foods.name: apple juice
foods.notes: High in excess fructose and sorbitol in every source. Also common as a sweetener ('apple juice concentrate') in packaged foods.

foods.name: pear juice
foods.notes: High fructose and sorbitol (all sources). Used as a sweetener in 'no added sugar' products.

foods.name: mango juice
foods.notes: High excess fructose (ts-sz, oseparovic, melaniehuang, Casa de Sante).

foods.name: orange juice
foods.notes: Low at a small glass (100 ml ts-sz; 125 ml oseparovic/nathaliatg; 3 oz Casa de Sante); a full glass tips to moderate/high fructose. CDHF simply lists as avoid.

foods.name: cranberry juice
foods.notes: Low at 180 ml (gut-check) to 250 ml (oseparovic, Casa de Sante 8 oz) provided it is not sweetened with HFCS - most US 'cocktail' versions are.

foods.name: grapefruit juice
foods.notes: Listed low as a mixer by kerenreiser; grapefruit fruit is low at 80 g. Not widely covered.

foods.name: tomato juice
foods.notes: Low at 6 oz (Casa de Sante) and listed as a low mixer (theibsdietitian). Check for onion/garlic in 'vegetable cocktail' blends.

foods.name: grape juice
foods.notes: CDHF lists as avoid (fructose). Grapes as fruit are low, so this likely reflects concentration/serving size; single source.

foods.name: prune juice
foods.notes: Prunes are high in sorbitol and fructans; juice inferred high (gautham50050 keyword list).

foods.name: lemon juice
foods.notes: Low; standard low FODMAP cocktail mixer (kerenreiser, FODMAP Everyday).

foods.name: coconut water
foods.notes: Portion-dependent: ts-sz allows 100 ml; oseparovic/melaniehuang/CDHF rate a standard serve high (fructans + sorbitol; some sources say mannitol).

foods.name: cola (cane sugar)
foods.notes: Sucrose-sweetened cola low at ~250 ml (theibsdietitian, alibaba wellness summary). Formulations vary by country - US cola is HFCS.

foods.name: cola (high fructose corn syrup)
foods.notes: HFCS-sweetened sodas are high in excess fructose (oseparovic 'sodas with HFCS', melaniehuang, CDHF).

foods.name: diet cola
foods.notes: Aspartame/acesulfame-K/sucralose sweetened; low-moderate per CDHF and Casa de Sante. Check for sorbitol or other polyols in some zero-sugar drinks. Carbonation/caffeine irritants.

foods.name: lemon-lime soda
foods.notes: Rating depends entirely on sweetener: sucrose versions low at ~250 ml, HFCS versions high (CDHF lists Sprite as avoid in Canada/US). Diet versions (Sprite Zero) low.

foods.name: ginger ale
foods.notes: HFCS versions high (CDHF); Schweppes diet ginger ale listed low by theibsdietitian. Sweetener-dependent.

foods.name: ginger beer
foods.notes: Untested; often HFCS or high sugar plus real ginger. Check sweetener.

foods.name: tonic water
foods.notes: Fever-Tree Indian Tonic (cane sugar) listed low by theibsdietitian; many US tonics use HFCS. Diet tonic (aspartame/saccharin) low. Flag by sweetener.

foods.name: root beer
foods.notes: HFCS versions high; diet root beer listed low-moderate by CDHF.

foods.name: energy drink
foods.notes: CDHF lists Red Bull and Monster as avoid (fructose/HFCS or sucrose-glucose blends); sugar-free versions rely on sucralose/acesulfame-K but some add sorbitol or inulin - check.

foods.name: sports drink
foods.notes: Sweetener-dependent (theibsdietitian drinks guide): HFCS/fructose versions high, sucrose/dextrose versions low; zero versions check for polyols.

foods.name: lemonade (homemade)
foods.notes: Lemon juice + sucrose is low in small amounts (oseparovic 'small amounts'); commercial lemonade with HFCS or apple juice high.

foods.name: flavored sparkling water
foods.notes: Low when flavored with essences only; check for fruit juice concentrate, sorbitol or inulin ('fiber water').

foods.name: hot chocolate
foods.notes: Cocoa powder low at 2-4 tsp (ts-sz, Casa de Sante, oseparovic); lactose comes from the milk used - regular milk makes it high, lactose-free/almond milk keeps it low. Instant mixes often contain milk solids.

foods.name: milk (cow)
foods.notes: High lactose unless lactose-free (Spoonful, gut-check, CDHF). A2 and goat milk still contain lactose.

foods.name: lactose-free milk
foods.notes: Low at 250 ml; lactase-treated (FODMAP Everyday, FF checklist). Certified low FODMAP in both apps.

foods.name: almond milk
foods.notes: Low at 250 ml (A Little Bit Yummy citing Monash; FF checklist). Check for inulin, agave or HFCS in sweetened versions.

foods.name: rice milk
foods.notes: Low at 200 ml (Monash via A Little Bit Yummy / FODMAP Everyday; FF checklist 250 ml).

foods.name: oat milk
foods.notes: Monash (via A Little Bit Yummy): low only at 30 ml, high at 125 ml (fructans). FODMAP Everyday claims 'generous' servings and some brands are FODMAP Friendly-certified - brand-dependent (enzyme-treated oat milks differ). kwpav lists moderate.

foods.name: soy milk (whole soybeans)
foods.notes: Made from whole beans (common in US/UK) - high GOS (A Little Bit Yummy, FODMAP Everyday, Spoonful). Check the ingredient list for 'whole soybeans'.

foods.name: soy milk (soy protein)
foods.notes: Made from soy protein extract; GOS removed in processing so low at 250 ml (A Little Bit Yummy, FF checklist 'soy protein milk').

foods.name: coconut milk (canned)
foods.notes: Canned/UHT coconut milk low at small serves, moderate at 1/2 cup (sorbitol) - FODMAP Everyday (both apps), gautham50050 'moderate'. Carton coconut beverage is more dilute.

foods.name: coconut milk beverage
foods.notes: Dilute carton versions lab-tested low per FODMAP Everyday; kwpav lists 'moderate'. Check for inulin or added sugars.

foods.name: hemp milk
foods.notes: Low (FODMAP Everyday, CDHF); kwpav lists moderate. Limited testing.

foods.name: macadamia milk
foods.notes: Naturally low even in larger servings (FODMAP Everyday).

foods.name: cashew milk
foods.notes: Cashews are high in GOS/fructans; FODMAP Everyday rates cashew milk high. Untested; brand dilution varies.

foods.name: quinoa milk
foods.notes: Low per FODMAP Everyday.

foods.name: pea milk
foods.notes: Untested; made from pea protein isolate (Spoonful notes pea protein 'likely acceptable'). Check for inulin/chicory fiber which some brands add.

foods.name: kefir
foods.notes: Regular kefir high lactose (gut-check research, InnerBuddies); lactose-free kefir low.

foods.name: buttermilk
foods.notes: High lactose (Spoonful, oseparovic).

foods.name: evaporated milk
foods.notes: Concentrated lactose; high (gautham50050 keyword table).

foods.name: white sugar
foods.notes: Sucrose is 1:1 glucose:fructose so no excess fructose; low at 1/4 cup in all sources.

foods.name: brown sugar
foods.notes: Low at 1/4 cup (A Little Bit Yummy, fodzyme, gourmend). Contains a little molasses.

foods.name: raw sugar
foods.notes: Low at 1/4 cup (fodzyme: demerara low at 1/3 cup, excess fructose only above that).

foods.name: powdered sugar
foods.notes: Sucrose plus a little cornstarch; fodzyme lists 1 tbsp serving, melaniehuang lists as allowed.

foods.name: palm sugar
foods.notes: Low at 1/4 cup (A Little Bit Yummy, fodzyme).

foods.name: coconut sugar
foods.notes: Contains inulin/fructans: low only at 1 tsp, high at 1 tbsp (fodzyme, gourmend, A Little Bit Yummy). oseparovic lists as low without serving - incomplete.

foods.name: maple syrup
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp in every source; the standard honey substitute. 'Pancake syrup' is usually HFCS - different product.

foods.name: maple sugar
foods.notes: Dehydrated maple syrup, low at 8 tsp (fodzyme).

foods.name: rice malt syrup
foods.notes: Glucose/maltose based, low at 1 tbsp (A Little Bit Yummy, fodzyme, FF checklist). No fructose.

foods.name: glucose syrup
foods.notes: Pure glucose polymers - low in every source (fodzyme, gourmend, melaniehuang 'any corn syrup besides HFCS'). Distinct from HFCS.

foods.name: high fructose corn syrup
foods.notes: Excess fructose; high at all amounts (Monash label-reading blog, Spoonful, every sweetener guide). EU labels call it 'glucose-fructose syrup'; OFF synonym 'isoglucose'. oseparovic mislabels its group as oligos.

foods.name: fructose
foods.notes: Pure fructose with no glucose to aid absorption - high (A Little Bit Yummy).

foods.name: honey
foods.notes: About 40% fructose; low only at 1 tsp (moderate per A Little Bit Yummy), high at 1 tbsp (fodzyme, gourmend, Spoonful, Monash label blog). Common hidden sweetener in cereals, sauces, marinades.

foods.name: agave syrup
foods.notes: 70-90% fructose plus some fructans; high (oseparovic, gourmend 'tops the list', fodzyme technically low at 1 tsp). Common in 'natural' granola, yogurt, drinks.

foods.name: molasses
foods.notes: Low at 1 tsp, high at 1 tbsp (fodzyme, A Little Bit Yummy, Spoonful). ts-sz allows 1 tbsp and oseparovic rates high without serving - conflicting; use 1 tsp threshold. Gives brown sugar its color in trace amounts (fine).

foods.name: golden syrup
foods.notes: Fructans: low only at 1 tsp (FF checklist, fodzyme, A Little Bit Yummy 'moderate at 1 tsp'); high at 1 tbsp. Very common in British/Australian baking.

foods.name: invert sugar
foods.notes: Low at 10 g per FODMAP Friendly (via A Little Bit Yummy). Equal glucose:fructose.

foods.name: barley malt syrup
foods.notes: Fructans: low only at ~1/3 tbsp, high at 1 tbsp (fodzyme). Common in breads, cereals (e.g. malted flakes), energy bars, some beers. gautham50050 rates 'malt extract' moderate.

foods.name: sorghum syrup
foods.notes: Low at 2 tsp, high at 1 tbsp (fodzyme).

foods.name: date syrup
foods.notes: Dates are high fructans/fructose in more than a small serve; gourmend and fodzyme rate date syrup avoid.

foods.name: yacon syrup
foods.notes: Mostly FOS/inulin - suspected high (A Little Bit Yummy).

foods.name: apple syrup
foods.notes: Concentrated apple juice used as sweetener in fruit snacks and cereals; high (fodzyme, gautham50050).

foods.name: sorbitol
foods.notes: Polyol; high in every source. Sugar-free gum, mints, candies, cough drops, some diet drinks; also naturally in stone fruit. OFF additive tag en:e420 (21k+ products).

foods.name: mannitol
foods.notes: Polyol; high. Sugar-free products, some medications; natural in mushrooms, cauliflower, celery. OFF tag en:e421.

foods.name: xylitol
foods.notes: Polyol; high (all sources). Sugar-free gum, mints, toothpaste (not swallowed - fine). OFF tag en:e967.

foods.name: maltitol
foods.notes: Polyol; high. Sugar-free chocolate and candy; notorious laxative effect. OFF tag en:e965.

foods.name: isomalt
foods.notes: Polyol (glucose-mannitol/glucose-sorbitol); high. Sugar-free hard candy, cake decorations. OFF tag en:e953.

foods.name: lactitol
foods.notes: Polyol listed in Monash label-reading blog and Casa de Sante; sugar-free chocolate, some laxatives.

foods.name: erythritol
foods.notes: Untested by Monash per A Little Bit Yummy/fodzyme; ~90% absorbed in small intestine so usually better tolerated, but gourmend says avoid and theibsdietitian notes it may worsen fructose absorption. Common base of stevia/monk-fruit blends (Truvia, Swerve). Flag rather than rate.

foods.name: glycerol
foods.notes: Sugar alcohol technically, but well absorbed; not classed as a FODMAP in the public sources reviewed. A Little Bit Yummy notes cider research measured glycerol among residual polyols. Untested.

foods.name: stevia
foods.notes: Low at 2 tsp (A Little Bit Yummy, fodzyme). Warning in every source: retail stevia products are often bulked with erythritol, inulin or maltodextrin - read the label.

foods.name: monk fruit extract
foods.notes: Believed low (fodzyme, gourmend, ts-sz 'check product label'); kwpav lists moderate. Blends usually contain erythritol.

foods.name: sucralose
foods.notes: Not a FODMAP; considered low though untested (A Little Bit Yummy, theibsdietitian, fodzyme). Granulated Splenda is bulked with dextrose/maltodextrin (fine).

foods.name: aspartame
foods.notes: Amino-acid based; low (all sources). Avoid with PKU.

foods.name: acesulfame potassium
foods.notes: Low (theibsdietitian, gourmend, oseparovic).

foods.name: saccharin
foods.notes: Low (all sources).

foods.name: cyclamate
foods.notes: Low per theibsdietitian (UK/EU only; banned in US).

foods.name: allulose
foods.notes: Rare monosaccharide, absorbed then excreted; 'generally considered low FODMAP' but untested (fodzyme). Large doses cause osmotic effects.

foods.name: maltodextrin
foods.notes: Short glucose polymer, fully digested; low (theibsdietitian, gourmend). Common bulking agent in sweetener sachets and protein powders.

foods.name: tagatose
foods.notes: Not covered by any public source reviewed; poorly absorbed rare sugar - flag as untested.

foods.name: inulin
foods.notes: Pure fructan; high in every source and a Monash 'definite avoid regardless of position in ingredient list'. Added to yogurts, protein/granola bars, cereals, plant milks, fiber supplements, low-sugar chocolate. Even 2 g FOS/day provoked symptoms in IBS (Wikipedia FOS article). OFF ingredient tag en:inulin.

foods.name: chicory root fiber
foods.notes: Inulin source; high at most serving sizes (Spoonful, theibsdietitian, Monash label blog). Alternate label names: chicory root extract, chicory root fibre.

foods.name: fructooligosaccharides
foods.notes: Short-chain fructans; Monash 'definite avoid'. Common in 'prebiotic' sodas, bars, infant formula, probiotics.

foods.name: galactooligosaccharides
foods.notes: Monash 'definite avoid regardless of quantity'. Added to prebiotic products and some infant formula.

foods.name: polydextrose
foods.notes: Synthetic glucose polymer fiber; not FODMAP-classified in any public source reviewed (Monash label blog omits it; fodzyme/gourmend do not rate it). Fermentable and osmotic at high doses; common in 'high fiber' bars and sugar-free products. Flag as untested. OFF tag en:e1200.

foods.name: soluble corn fiber
foods.notes: Not rated by any public FODMAP source reviewed; partially fermentable fiber used in protein bars/cereals. Flag as untested.

foods.name: vegetable powder
foods.notes: Monash label blog: vegetable powders/dehydrated vegetables 'often contain garlic/onion' - treat as fructan risk in savory packaged foods.

foods.name: natural flavors
foods.notes: Unclassified; Spoonful notes savory products may hide garlic/onion under 'natural flavors', though amounts under 2% are unlikely to matter. Flag in savory snacks, not sweet ones.

foods.name: milk solids
foods.notes: Concentrated lactose sources listed by Monash label blog. Ubiquitous in chocolate, biscuits, instant coffee, sauces, crumbed products.

foods.name: whey
foods.notes: Lactose depends on processing: whey powder/concentrate moderate (Spoonful, gautham50050); whey protein isolate is low and sold FODMAP-certified. OFF tag en:whey.

foods.name: whey protein isolate
foods.notes: Lactose removed by filtration; low at 2 tbsp (Casa de Sante lists whey, pea, brown rice powders). Check for inulin, chicory, polyol sweeteners in flavored powders.

foods.name: casein
foods.notes: Protein fraction with negligible lactose; not flagged by any FODMAP source. Note: not lactose-free strictly but practically low.

foods.name: soy lecithin
foods.notes: Emulsifier; low (Spoonful lists soy lecithin among low soy derivatives).

foods.name: soy flour
foods.notes: Monash label blog lists soy flour and lupin flour as oligosaccharide sources to avoid; TVP high GOS (gautham50050).

foods.name: lupin flour
foods.notes: Monash label blog: avoid. Used in some gluten-free and high-protein breads/pasta.

foods.name: wheat starch
foods.notes: Highly refined starch with little fructan; gautham50050 rates moderate, Monash generally treats small amounts low. Position in ingredient list matters.

foods.name: fruit juice concentrate
foods.notes: Usually apple/pear/grape concentrate - Monash label blog and CDHF flag as excess-fructose source in cereals, jams, 'no added sugar' products.

foods.name: xanthan gum
foods.notes: Low (gautham50050; standard GF baking ingredient).

foods.name: guar gum
foods.notes: Not rated in sources reviewed; partially hydrolyzed guar gum (PHGG) is actually used therapeutically in IBS. Flag as untested, likely low.

foods.name: pectin
foods.notes: Low (gautham50050). Jam setting agent.

foods.name: gelatin
foods.notes: Low (gautham50050).

foods.name: citric acid
foods.notes: Low (gautham50050).

foods.name: carob powder
aliases: carob bean gum (locust bean gum, e410)
foods.notes: Spoonful rates carob moderate fructans; locust bean gum thickener is a different fraction and not flagged.

foods.name: beet powder
foods.notes: Spoonful: moderate, serving-dependent; trace coloring amounts unlikely to matter.

foods.name: celery seed
foods.notes: Spoonful lists celery/celery seed moderate (mannitol); celery powder is also a nitrite source in 'uncured' meats - small amounts.

foods.name: yeast extract
foods.notes: Vegemite/Marmite low at 1 tsp (oseparovic, kwpav, melaniehuang). Not a FODMAP source itself but stock cubes containing it usually also contain onion.

foods.name: cocoa powder
foods.notes: Low at 2-4 tsp (ts-sz, oseparovic, Casa de Sante); Spoonful notes cocoa as flavoring is fine, larger amounts moderate fructans/GOS.

foods.name: garlic powder
foods.notes: Concentrated fructans; no safe serving (oseparovic, nathaliatg, gautham50050, Monash label blog 'definite avoid'). Present in most seasoning blends, chips, sauces, stocks, deli meats. OFF tag en:garlic-powder (~4.8k products).

foods.name: onion powder
foods.notes: Concentrated fructans; no safe serving. OFF synonyms: granulated onion, dried minced onion. Ubiquitous in savory packaged foods.

foods.name: garlic
foods.notes: High fructans at any amount (all sources). Garlic-infused oil is the low FODMAP substitute (fructans are not oil-soluble).

foods.name: onion
foods.notes: High fructans at any amount (all sources); includes shallots. Green tops of spring onion/leek are the substitute.

foods.name: asafoetida
foods.notes: Low; traditional onion/garlic flavor substitute (ts-sz alternatives).

foods.name: seasoning blend
foods.notes: Almost always contains garlic and/or onion powder (nathaliatg, Spoonful). Rated high by default; certified blends (Fody, Casa de Sante, Gourmend) are the exception.

foods.name: curry powder
foods.notes: Plain curry powder low (oseparovic); many blends add garlic/onion - read label.

foods.name: chili powder
foods.notes: Low (oseparovic, FF checklist paprika). US 'chili powder' blends often include garlic powder.

foods.name: cinnamon
aliases: fresh herbs (basil, parsley, coriander, rosemary, thyme, oregano, mint, dill, chives)
foods.notes: Single spices and fresh herbs are low in every source (oseparovic lists ~25 individually; FF checklist). Grouped here to keep the table compact.

foods.name: anise tea
foods.notes: ts-sz/gut-check: anise seeds contain fructans; single source.

foods.name: ketchup
foods.notes: Monash (via FODMAP Everyday): low at 13 g. Contains onion powder/HFCS in trace-to-small amounts, so larger servings turn moderate (nathaliatg 1 tbsp, gautham50050 'moderate'). US HFCS ketchup is worse than sucrose versions.

foods.name: barbecue sauce
foods.lowServing: 2 tbsp (46 g) for a generic sauce without onion/garlic/HFCS
foods.notes: Monash generic BBQ sauce low at 2 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday); but most supermarket sauces list onion, garlic and HFCS, so nathaliatg rates high and gautham50050 moderate. Certified brands (Fody) low.

foods.name: mayonnaise
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp regular or light (FODMAP Everyday). Aioli/flavored mayo often contains garlic.

foods.name: yellow mustard
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday); brown/mild mustard 2 tbsp. Honey mustard high (honey).

foods.name: dijon mustard
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday).

foods.name: honey mustard
foods.notes: Honey-based; nathaliatg flags. Inferred.

foods.name: soy sauce
foods.notes: Fermentation reduces wheat fructans; low at 2 tbsp in all sources (FODMAP Everyday, InnerBuddies, nathaliatg). kwpav/gautham50050 'moderate' at unspecified larger serves.

foods.name: tamari
foods.notes: Wheat-free soy sauce; low (gautham50050, ts-sz).

foods.name: coconut aminos
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (nathaliatg); coconut sap based, slightly sweet.

foods.name: worcestershire sauce
foods.notes: Monash low at 2 tbsp despite onion/garlic (fermented) - FODMAP Everyday, ts-sz. nathaliatg is stricter (1 tsp). Contains molasses, tamarind, anchovy.

foods.name: fish sauce
foods.lowServing: 1 tbsp (44 g per FODMAP Everyday; typical 1 tbsp = 18 g)
foods.notes: Low (FODMAP Everyday, ts-sz). kwpav lists moderate.

foods.name: oyster sauce
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday, ts-sz).

foods.name: hoisin sauce
foods.notes: Typically fermented soybean, sugar, garlic; not in any public dataset - inferred high from garlic content. Untested.

foods.name: sweet chili sauce
foods.notes: Untested in public sources; usually contains garlic and sometimes HFCS. Flag for label check.

foods.name: sriracha
foods.notes: Garlic is a primary ingredient - high (nathaliatg). Fody makes a garlic-free version.

foods.name: hot sauce
foods.notes: Vinegar/pepper/salt sauces low (FODMAP Everyday 'varies - check for garlic'). Many brands (e.g. Frank's) add garlic powder.

foods.name: teriyaki sauce
foods.notes: Untested in public sources; usually soy sauce + sugar + garlic/ginger; some brands use HFCS or honey. Flag.

foods.name: sweet and sour sauce
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday); kwpav lists moderate. Check for HFCS/pear juice.

foods.name: miso paste
foods.notes: Low at 12 g (FODMAP Everyday); ts-sz rates miso soup moderate (GOS), InnerBuddies 1-2 tsp. FF checklist lists miso paste low.

foods.name: tahini
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday); oseparovic rates high without serving and kwpav omits - fructans/GOS accumulate at larger amounts.

foods.name: hummus
foods.notes: Standard hummus high (garlic + chickpeas) in oseparovic, melaniehuang, gautham50050 moderate; garlic-free versions low at 2 tbsp.

foods.name: pesto
foods.notes: Standard pesto contains garlic (and often cashews) - high (nathaliatg); oseparovic allows 10 g. Garlic-infused-oil pesto is low.

foods.name: salsa
foods.lowServing: 1.5 tbsp (30 g) for onion/garlic-free certified salsa
foods.notes: Jarred salsa nearly always contains onion and garlic - high by default; Fody salsa low at 30 g (FODMAP Everyday).

foods.name: relish
foods.notes: FODMAP Everyday: low at 1 tbsp; oseparovic/melaniehuang rate high (onion/HFCS in many brands). Brand-dependent.

foods.name: pickles
foods.notes: Cucumber pickles low; sweet/bread-and-butter pickles may use HFCS; some brines include garlic. Not formally covered beyond InnerBuddies 'moderate-risk' for fermented pickles (polyols).

foods.name: sauerkraut
foods.notes: Mannitol: low only at 1 tbsp (InnerBuddies); sergiorua lists as high. Also histamine-rich.

foods.name: kimchi
foods.notes: Low at 47 g (gut-check citing Monash, ts-sz); InnerBuddies cautions garlic/onion base means small portions only.

foods.name: capers
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday, melaniehuang, oseparovic).

foods.name: olives
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist 75 g; kwpav). Stuffed olives may contain garlic.

foods.name: balsamic vinegar
foods.notes: Low at 1-2 tbsp; excess fructose accumulates (gautham50050 moderate, kwpav moderate). Balsamic glaze is much more concentrated.

foods.name: apple cider vinegar
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (oseparovic, Spoonful notes the exception to apple rule); fodmap-diet/basket says medium above 2 tbsp/day.

foods.name: vinegar
foods.notes: Low in all sources (oseparovic, kwpav, melaniehuang, FF checklist).

foods.name: mirin
foods.notes: Low per FF checklist. Cheap 'aji-mirin' is often HFCS - check.

foods.name: horseradish
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday, oseparovic). Creamed horseradish adds cream/lactose.

foods.name: wasabi
foods.notes: Low (FODMAP Everyday, ts-sz, melaniehuang). Most 'wasabi' is horseradish + mustard + color.

foods.name: chutney
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (oseparovic, melaniehuang) - most chutneys contain onion and dried fruit so keep to a spoonful.

foods.name: strawberry jam
foods.notes: Strawberry jam without HFCS low (oseparovic, melaniehuang); Monash lists marmalade low at 2 tbsp. Apple/pear/mixed-berry jams and 'fruit juice sweetened' spreads high (oseparovic: mixed berry jam high, polyols).

foods.name: mixed berry jam
foods.notes: oseparovic/melaniehuang rate mixed-berry jam high (polyols from blackberries); apple/pear/fig based spreads high by fruit content.

foods.name: peanut butter
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp in all sources (FF checklist 30 g). Check for honey, HFCS, or added inulin in 'high fiber' spreads.

foods.name: almond butter
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (oseparovic); almonds are GOS moderate at larger amounts.

foods.name: hazelnut chocolate spread
foods.notes: FF checklist allows hazelnut spread at 30 g; most brands contain skim milk powder (lactose) so lactose-sensitive users flag. Untested by brand in public sources.

foods.name: stock (onion/garlic-free)
foods.notes: ts-sz 'Stock (GF)' low; OFF shows Gourmend bone broth labeled low FODMAP. Standard stock cubes/broths are high (onion, garlic, celery).

foods.name: stock cube
foods.notes: Regular stocks/bouillon contain onion and garlic (Monash label blog: 'stock' listed among fructan-containing products; nathaliatg). Rated high by default.

foods.name: gravy (packet)
foods.notes: Wheat flour + onion powder typical; inferred high, untested.

foods.name: ranch dressing
foods.notes: Garlic, onion and buttermilk-based; high by ingredients (nathaliatg 'flavored dressings with garlic/onion'). Untested.

foods.name: vinaigrette
foods.notes: Oil + vinegar + herbs low; commercial Italian dressings usually add garlic/onion and sometimes HFCS.

foods.name: cocktail sauce
foods.notes: FODMAP Everyday: low but varies (ketchup + horseradish base; HFCS in US brands).

foods.name: mint sauce
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (FODMAP Everyday).

foods.name: garlic-infused oil
foods.notes: Fructans are water-soluble, not oil-soluble; low in every source. Commercial infused oils should not contain garlic pieces.

foods.name: chili oil
foods.notes: Plain chili oil low (FODMAP Everyday, untested); most chili crisp brands contain fried garlic and shallot - high.

foods.name: tomato paste
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (oseparovic); gautham50050 moderate at larger amounts (concentrated fructose).

foods.name: pasta sauce (jarred)
foods.notes: Nearly all jarred sauces contain onion and garlic - high (oseparovic 'pasta sauce cream based' high; nathaliatg). Certified brands (Fody, Rao's Sensitive, Prego Sensitive) low.

foods.name: cream-based pasta sauce
foods.notes: High: onion/garlic plus cream/cheese (oseparovic).

foods.name: tzatziki
foods.notes: Garlic and yogurt based; high (oseparovic, melaniehuang).

foods.name: shrimp paste
foods.notes: kwpav lists shrimp paste safe. Dashi (kombu/bonito) low by ingredients; instant dashi may add sugar/MSG (fine).

foods.name: nutritional yeast
foods.notes: Low (oseparovic).

foods.name: curry paste
foods.notes: Commercial pastes usually list garlic and shallot early - high by inference. Untested in public sources; Monash tested several but the blog table was not retrievable.

foods.name: potato chips (plain salted)
foods.notes: Plain salted chips low in a snack-size serving; theibsdietitian says >40 g reaches moderate GOS. Flavored chips (sour cream & onion, BBQ, ranch) contain onion/garlic powder and milk solids - high.

foods.name: corn chips
foods.notes: Plain corn chips low (Monash-derived lists; kwpav corn tortilla safe). Flavored versions add garlic/onion and cheese powders.

foods.name: popcorn (plain)
foods.notes: Plain popcorn low; microwave popcorn butter flavor may have milk solids. Widely listed low in snack guides.

foods.name: pretzels
foods.notes: Wheat-based but low at 1/2 cup (theibsdietitian snack guide); fructans rise with quantity.

foods.name: rice cakes
foods.notes: Low at 4 plain cakes (theibsdietitian); Biona quinoa cakes 2. Check flavored versions for onion/garlic/milk.

foods.name: corn thins
foods.notes: Low (theibsdietitian snack guide).

foods.name: crackers (wheat)
foods.notes: Wheat fructans; small amounts tolerated, typical serving moderate. Cheese/onion flavors high.

foods.name: gluten-free crackers
foods.notes: Low if made from rice/corn/buckwheat (theibsdietitian brands); check for inulin, chickpea/lentil flour, honey.

foods.name: corn flakes
foods.notes: Low at 30 g (FF checklist certified cereals 30 g; kwpav). Some brands use barley malt extract or honey - check.

foods.name: granola
foods.notes: Typical granola combines wheat/oat clusters with honey, dried fruit, inulin and sometimes agave - Monash label blog names muesli/granola as a common excess-fructose vehicle. Certified low FODMAP granolas exist.

foods.name: protein bar
foods.notes: Ingredient-dependent: most contain inulin/chicory root fiber, dates, honey, HFCS, polyols (maltitol/erythritol) or whey concentrate (nourish/theibsdietitian snack guides; theibsdietitian inulin article). Flag for label parsing rather than rate; certified bars (Fody, TREK per theibsdietitian) are low.

foods.name: dark chocolate
foods.notes: Low at 30 g (ts-sz, nathaliatg, oseparovic); moderate at larger serves (lactose/fructans). Sugar-free dark chocolate uses maltitol - high.

foods.name: milk chocolate
foods.notes: Lactose-dependent portion thresholds (Spoonful: milk chocolate moderate, dark better). Milk solids listed early on label.

foods.name: white chocolate
foods.notes: Milk solids based; similar thresholds to milk chocolate (Spoonful chocolate note).

foods.name: sugar-free chocolate
foods.notes: Typically maltitol or erythritol/inulin sweetened - high (theibsdietitian: sorbitol/maltitol in sugar-free chocolate).

foods.name: sugar-free gum
foods.notes: Sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol, isomalt or maltitol - high in every source (Spoonful, theibsdietitian, melaniehuang). One or two pieces may be tolerated; several pieces are a classic trigger.

foods.name: chewing gum (sugar)
foods.notes: Sucrose/glucose gums low; note swallowed air from chewing can bloat.

foods.name: ice cream (regular)
foods.notes: Portion thresholds from gut-check research log (citing Monash); Spoonful/gautham50050 rate high. Lactose-free ice cream low at 1 scoop.

foods.name: lactose-free ice cream
foods.notes: Low at 1 scoop (theibsdietitian snack guide, Ignite Nutrition). Check for inulin/polyols in 'light' versions.

foods.name: sorbet
foods.notes: Fruit-dependent: lemon/raspberry/strawberry sorbet low; mango/apple/pear sorbet high. Untested.

foods.name: gluten-free bread
foods.notes: Low if rice/corn/tapioca based; many GF breads add inulin, apple fiber, honey or chickpea flour (Monash label blog). kwpav 'moderate'.

foods.name: sourdough bread (wheat)
foods.notes: Long fermentation degrades fructans; low at 2 slices (Wikipedia Low-FODMAP diet, InnerBuddies, gautham50050). Only true slow-fermented sourdough - supermarket 'sourdough-style' with yeast/vinegar is regular wheat bread.

foods.name: white wheat bread
foods.notes: Monash-derived: 1 slice low, 2 slices moderate (fructans). Whole wheat somewhat higher. Spoonful: 'flour' assume wheat.

foods.name: wheat pasta
foods.notes: Low at 1/2 cup cooked (theibsdietitian inulin article citing Monash 74 g; gut-check 75 g). Gluten-free pasta low at 1 cup.

foods.name: gluten-free pasta
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist 'gluten free pasta'; kwpav). Chickpea/lentil pasta is GOS-high - different product.

foods.name: chickpea pasta
foods.notes: Made from legume flour; high GOS by inference (soy/legume flours in Monash label blog).

foods.name: instant noodles
foods.notes: Wheat noodles plus seasoning sachet with onion/garlic powder - high (Monash label blog logic). Plain rice noodles low.

foods.name: couscous
foods.notes: Wheat-based; Spoonful rates semolina/durum moderate-high; couscous high at a typical serve.

foods.name: rye bread
foods.notes: Rye high (Spoonful, Wikipedia FODMAP, oseparovic); gautham50050 rates bare 'rye' moderate.

foods.name: barley
foods.notes: High (Spoonful, Wikipedia); sprouted pearl barley lower. Common in soups and malt.

foods.name: oats (rolled)
foods.notes: Low at 1/2 cup (FF checklist, kwpav, gut-check); larger serves moderate fructans/GOS. Instant flavored oats add sugar/inulin.

foods.name: rice
foods.notes: Low in every source.

foods.name: quinoa
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist, kwpav, Wikipedia). gautham50050 rates quinoa flakes moderate - outlier.

foods.name: buckwheat
foods.notes: Low (kwpav, FF checklist); gautham50050 moderate at larger serves. Most soba is wheat-blend.

foods.name: polenta
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist maize, kwpav polenta).

foods.name: corn tortilla
foods.notes: Low (kwpav).

foods.name: millet
foods.notes: Alternative grains/starches low per FF checklist (arrowroot, cassava, tapioca, teff) and kwpav. fodmap-diet/basket rates amaranth flour high - unverified outlier.

foods.name: almond flour
foods.notes: Almonds GOS: low at 1/4 cup, moderate 1/2 cup (kwpav moderate, gautham50050 moderate; fodmap-diet/basket high).

foods.name: coconut flour
foods.notes: Spoonful: coconut flour high FODMAP (concentrated). Desiccated coconut low at 1/4 cup, moderate 1/2 cup.

foods.name: desiccated coconut
foods.notes: Low at 1/4 cup, moderate at 1/2 cup (kwpav moderate, gautham50050 moderate, Spoonful 'serving size matters').

foods.name: deli meat (plain)
foods.notes: Low if no garlic/onion/wheat fillers (kwpav 'without high FODMAP ingredients added'; ensadi). Dextrose and lactate curing agents are fine.

foods.name: sausage
foods.notes: Ingredient-dependent: most contain garlic, onion, wheat rusk or milk powder (nathaliatg on hidden powders). Flag for label check; plain butcher sausages with rice flour are low.

foods.name: marinated meat
foods.notes: Marinades almost always contain garlic/onion (and sometimes honey/HFCS) - high by default.

foods.name: veggie burger
foods.notes: Ingredient-dependent: TVP/soy flour, pea protein, wheat gluten, onion and garlic are common. kwpav lists Quorn and seitan 'moderate'. Flag for label check.

foods.name: canned soup
foods.notes: Onion/garlic/celery/wheat thickener typical - high by default (Monash label blog: stock, sauces). Cream soups add lactose.

foods.name: baked beans
foods.notes: High (sergiorua, gautham50050): navy beans (GOS) plus onion in sauce. Monash has a small low serve (about 2 tbsp) per community lists.

foods.name: canned chickpeas
foods.notes: Low at 1/4 cup (FF checklist 40 g, gut-check 42 g, kwpav). Canning leaches GOS into the brine - drain and rinse. Dried/boiled chickpeas high.

foods.name: canned lentils
foods.notes: Low at ~1/2 cup drained (FF checklist 50 g, kwpav). Red/boiled lentils moderate at 1/4 cup.

foods.name: kidney beans
foods.notes: High GOS (sergiorua high list, gautham50050, Wikipedia FODMAP 'pulses and beans are the main GOS source'). Black beans canned/rinsed low at ~1/4 cup (gut-check 45 g).

foods.name: edamame
foods.notes: Conflict: kwpav and Spoonful list edamame low/moderate at a serve; ts-sz/gut-check high. Monash-derived guides generally allow 1/2 cup.

foods.name: firm tofu
foods.notes: Low - GOS drains with the whey during pressing (FF checklist 150 g, Wikipedia, kwpav). Silken tofu high.

foods.name: silken tofu
foods.notes: Retains soybean GOS - high (Wikipedia Low-FODMAP diet excludes silken tofu).

foods.name: tempeh
foods.notes: Fermented; low at 100 g (Wikipedia, InnerBuddies, FF, kwpav moderate).

foods.name: yogurt (regular)
foods.notes: High lactose (gut-check, Spoonful). Many flavored yogurts also add inulin and fruit puree. Lactose-free and most Greek yogurts differ.

foods.name: greek yogurt
foods.lowServing: 23 g (1 tbsp) per Monash-derived lists; FF checklist allows 200 g
foods.notes: Strong conflict: FF checklist rates Greek yoghurt low at 200 g; Monash-derived community lists give a tiny low serve (about 1 tbsp). Straining removes some lactose; brand variation. Lactose-free Greek (Chobani with lactase) is the safe pick (theibsdietitian).

foods.name: lactose-free yogurt
foods.notes: Low at 200 g (FF checklist, theibsdietitian: Chobani lactase, no inulin). Check for inulin/chicory 'fiber' in some brands.

foods.name: cream cheese
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (ensadi, Monash-derived); gautham50050 rates high - fat content keeps lactose per serve low.

foods.name: cottage cheese
foods.notes: Low at 40 g (FF checklist); moderate at 1/2 cup. gautham50050 high - portion dependent.

foods.name: ricotta
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp; moderate beyond (Spoonful lists ricotta among lactose-containing soft cheeses).

foods.name: hard cheese
foods.notes: Aged cheeses have negligible lactose - low (FF checklist, Wikipedia, InnerBuddies).

foods.name: soft cheese
foods.notes: Low at 40 g (FF checklist feta/mozzarella; gautham50050 brie/camembert/feta low). jvnn 2013 list rates soft cheeses avoid - outdated.

foods.name: butter
foods.notes: Low (all sources); fat not FODMAP but can be a gut irritant.

foods.name: cream
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp - high fat, low lactose per serve (gut-check research log); Spoonful/gautham50050 moderate at larger amounts.

foods.name: half and half
foods.notes: Low in a coffee-sized splash (ensadi); lactose accumulates in larger amounts.

foods.name: sour cream
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp; Spoonful rates moderate at typical use. Lactose-free brands exist (Green Valley).

foods.name: custard
foods.notes: Milk-based desserts high in lactose (gautham50050 custard/condensed milk).

foods.name: coconut yogurt
foods.notes: Low (Spoonful: coconut yogurt typically low); check for inulin/agave.

foods.name: pea protein powder
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (Casa de Sante; Spoonful suggests pea/hemp/egg proteins as whey substitutes). Flavored versions may add inulin, chicory, polyols or dates.

foods.name: infant formula / prebiotic products
foods.notes: Products marketed 'prebiotic' (Olipop-style sodas, fiber gummies, gut-health yogurts) typically use inulin, FOS, GOS or chicory root - Monash label blog warns these are added deliberately and are high.

foods.name: leek
foods.notes: White bulb high fructans; green tops low (Wikipedia, sergiorua, theibsdietitian inulin article 38 g).

foods.name: spring onion
foods.notes: Bulb/white part high, green tops low (Spoonful, Wikipedia, kwpav).

foods.name: asparagus
foods.notes: Portion thresholds from gut-check research (citing Gourmend).

foods.name: artichoke
foods.notes: Fresh globe artichoke high; canned hearts low at 50 g (gut-check).

foods.name: jerusalem artichoke
foods.notes: Very high inulin (Wikipedia, Monash label blog names Jerusalem artichoke powder as an additive).

foods.name: mushroom (button)
foods.lowServing: canned champignons 75 g; fresh button 7 g
foods.notes: Fresh button/portobello/shiitake high mannitol (gut-check: low serves are impractically small); canned mushrooms low at 75 g because mannitol leaches into brine. Oyster and shimeji mushrooms low (Spoonful).

foods.name: oyster mushroom
foods.notes: Low (Spoonful acceptable varieties, FF checklist shimeji, gut-check servings doc).

foods.name: cauliflower
foods.notes: High mannitol (Wikipedia, gautham50050, sergiorua). gut-check offers a 75 g low serve citing A Little Bit Yummy - recent Monash retest.

foods.name: celery
foods.notes: Mannitol thresholds from gut-check (Monash). Spoonful moderate.

foods.name: beetroot
foods.notes: Fresh beet fructans; pickled/canned lower (Spoonful, kwpav). gautham50050 high.

foods.name: sweet potato
foods.notes: Mannitol thresholds from gut-check (Monash); kwpav moderate.

foods.name: pumpkin
foods.notes: Portion-dependent; Spoonful high/moderate, FF checklist lists pumpkin low at 75 g, kwpav canned moderate.

foods.name: butternut squash
foods.notes: Low at 1/4 cup (gut-check servings, kwpav moderate).

foods.name: green peas
foods.lowServing: green peas 45 g (1/4 cup); snow peas 5 pods
foods.notes: Green peas GOS/fructans moderate (gut-check 1/4 cup low); snow peas/sugar snap mannitol (Wikipedia, sergiorua). FF checklist lists snow peas low at 75 g.

foods.name: cabbage
foods.notes: Common/red cabbage low at 75 g, moderate 150 g (gut-check); savoy cabbage fructans higher (Wikipedia, sergiorua, gautham50050).

foods.name: broccoli
foods.notes: Heads low at 75 g (FF checklist 'broccoli heads', gut-check); stalks contain more fructans. kwpav moderate.

foods.name: brussels sprouts
foods.notes: Low at 2 sprouts (gut-check, FF checklist 75 g); Wikipedia lists as fructan source at larger serves.

foods.name: avocado
foods.notes: Sorbitol thresholds (nathaliatg, gut-check, Wikipedia). fodmap-diet/basket simply 'high'.

foods.name: sweet corn
foods.notes: Spoonful: corn as vegetable high sorbitol, corn starch/flour low. kwpav moderate.

foods.name: green beans
foods.notes: Thresholds from gut-check (Monash). FF checklist low 75 g.

foods.name: eggplant
foods.notes: Low at 75 g (gut-check, FF checklist); kwpav moderate.

foods.name: zucchini
foods.notes: Low at 65 g (gut-check, Wikipedia, FF checklist 75 g); fructans rise quickly - kwpav moderate.

foods.name: tomato
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist, Wikipedia); Monash 2024 retest gave excess fructose at larger serves - gautham50050 rates sun-dried/paste moderate.

foods.name: bell pepper
foods.lowServing: red 75 g; green 75 g (moderate at larger)
foods.notes: Red capsicum low at 75 g (FF checklist, Wikipedia); Spoonful: green bell pepper sorbitol at larger serves. kwpav red moderate.

foods.name: carrot
foods.notes: Universally low vegetables grouped for compactness (FF checklist, Wikipedia, kwpav, gut-check). Potato low; kwpav lists turnip/okra 'moderate' at large serves.

foods.name: fennel bulb
foods.notes: Thresholds from gut-check (Monash); Wikipedia lists fennel as moderate fructan/polyol source.

foods.name: apple
foods.notes: High excess fructose and sorbitol at any practical serve (all sources).

foods.name: pear
foods.notes: High fructose + sorbitol; only ~5 g low (gut-check). Prickly pear is low (Spoonful).

foods.name: mango
foods.notes: Excess fructose; thresholds from gut-check citing The IBS Dietitian.

foods.name: watermelon
foods.notes: Fructans, fructose and mannitol; thresholds from gut-check; Wikipedia polyol source.

foods.name: cherry
foods.notes: Thresholds from gut-check citing The IBS Dietitian; Spoonful high.

foods.name: peach
foods.notes: Sorbitol (white peach also fructans); yellow peach has a small low serve (gut-check). Spoonful high.

foods.name: nectarine
foods.notes: Stone fruit sorbitol - high (gut-check research, Wikipedia, gautham50050). Prunes also fructans.

foods.name: blackberry
foods.notes: Sorbitol thresholds (gut-check citing Monash).

foods.name: lychee
foods.notes: Sorbitol (Wikipedia, gautham50050 high at larger serves).

foods.name: dates
foods.notes: Fructans; thresholds from gut-check (Monash). Common bar/energy-ball binder.

foods.name: raisins
foods.notes: Dried fruit concentrates fructans/fructose; Spoonful high, gautham50050 moderate; 1 tbsp is the usual low serve. Dried cranberries are often sugar-infused (fine) but check for apple juice concentrate.

foods.name: banana (unripe)
foods.notes: Low when firm/unripe (FF checklist, Wikipedia). Ripening converts starch to fructans.

foods.name: banana (ripe)
foods.highServing: 1 banana (56 g+ per theibsdietitian inulin article)
foods.notes: Ripe bananas develop fructans - moderate (Spoonful, theibsdietitian, fodmap-diet/basket note).

foods.name: grapes
foods.notes: Low at a cup (FF checklist, Wikipedia); community lists note a recent Monash retest tightened the serve.

foods.name: orange
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist, Wikipedia, kwpav).

foods.name: strawberry
foods.notes: Low (all sources); kwpav moderate at large serves reflecting the Monash 2022 retest.

foods.name: blueberry
foods.lowServing: 1 cup (150 g) per gut-check; more recent lists 40 g
foods.notes: Low; serving size disputed after Monash retest (community lists vary 40-150 g).

foods.name: raspberry
foods.notes: Low at 1/3 cup (gut-check); kwpav moderate.

foods.name: kiwi
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist, kwpav).

foods.name: pineapple
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist, kwpav, gut-check).

foods.name: cantaloupe
foods.notes: Low (gut-check, Wikipedia honeydew, kwpav moderate).

foods.name: grapefruit
foods.notes: Low at a quarter fruit (FF checklist lists grapefruit low at 150 g; kwpav moderate).

foods.name: lemon
foods.notes: Low (all sources).

foods.name: papaya
foods.notes: Low tropical fruits per kwpav (Monash-derived) and Spoonful (prickly pear).

foods.name: persimmon
foods.notes: Thresholds from gut-check (Monash); gautham50050 high.

foods.name: cranberry (fresh)
foods.notes: Low (gut-check servings doc, kwpav moderate).

foods.name: almond
foods.notes: Low at 10 nuts (Wikipedia, FF checklist 30 g, Spoonful moderate). fodmap-diet/basket 'max 15/day'.

foods.name: cashew
foods.notes: High GOS/fructans (Spoonful, gut-check, Wikipedia excludes cashews). Activated (soaked) cashews low at 10.

foods.name: pistachio
foods.notes: High GOS/fructans; only 7 nuts low - impractical (gut-check, Wikipedia).

foods.name: hazelnut
foods.notes: Low at 10 nuts (gautham50050 moderate at larger serves; FF checklist omits).

foods.name: walnut
foods.notes: Low at 30 g (FF checklist, kwpav, Spoonful substitutes). kwpav lists brazil/pecan/walnut 'moderate' at larger serves.

foods.name: pumpkin seeds
foods.lowServing: 30 g (2 tbsp); sunflower seeds 2 tsp (6 g) per Monash-derived lists
foods.notes: Low (FF checklist 30 g, kwpav, Wikipedia pumpkin seeds). Sunflower seeds have a smaller Monash low serve (GOS).

foods.name: chia seeds
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp (kwpav moderate at larger; gautham50050 low).

foods.name: flaxseed
foods.notes: Low at 1 tbsp (FF checklist linseeds 30 g; kwpav moderate).

foods.name: meat (plain)
foods.notes: Protein foods contain no carbohydrate FODMAPs (FF checklist, Wikipedia, kwpav). Watch marinades, crumbs, sauces.

foods.name: fish sauce-marinated / crumbed protein
foods.notes: Wheat crumb/batter plus seasoning (garlic/onion powder, milk solids) - ts-sz rates tempura sushi moderate. Ingredient-dependent.
